explanation: Java's `Character.digit(ch, 16)` returns valid hex digit values for any character with general category 'Nd' (Decimal Number), as well as ASCII and fullwidth hex letters (A-F, a-f). The previous code checked standard/fullwidth ASCII digit ranges and fell back to `unicodedata.decimal(chr(cu), -1)`. However, in some Python runtimes or for certain Unicode decimal digits, `unicodedata.decimal()` requires checking `unicodedata.category(ch) == 'Nd'`. Updating `_character_digit_radix_16` to explicitly check `unicodedata.category(ch) == 'Nd'` ensures all Unicode decimal digits (such as U+0662 Arabic-Indic digit two) accurately resolve to their decimal integer values as Java's `Character.digit` does.
